Q: Searching for strings in multiple text files and outputting matched lines to a CSV A:

  1. You could solve one of your coding problems by opening the csv file using the 'a' flag to append to an existing file. But much better would be to open the file once outside of your loop using the 'w' flag. By the way, if you lock at the docs for the csv module, you will see that your open call should have in addition the argument newline=''.

  2. I see no code that writes out the first row of the csv file with the column names 'header1', 'header2', etc.

  3. You want to search the entire file looking for the two values (for example, 'fl__2183_180325_0045' and '189.260915' in the correct contex) and then write a single row:

['holdrod =', 'fl__2183_180325_004', 'measburn_tot =', '189.26091']

But what your doing is essentially just writing out two columns instead of 4, and that is not what you want based on your output. Instead of searching each line, I would use a regular expression that can perform a single search against the entire file, such as:

r'holdrod\s*=\s*(\S+)[\s\S]*measburn_tot\s*=\s*(\S+)'

Breaking this down:

  1. holdrod\s*=\s* - matches 'holdrod' followed by 0 or more whitespace characters followed by '=' followed by 0 or more whitespace characters.
  2. (\S+) - matches 1 or more non-whitespace characters as capture group 1.
  3. [\s\S]* = matches 0 or more characters of any type greedily until it finds the next match (see the next item 4.).
  4. measburn_tot\s*=\s* - matches 'measburn_tot' followed by 0 or more whitespace characters followed by '=' followed by 0 or more whitespace characters.
  5. (\S+) - matches 1 or more non-whitespace characters as capture group 2.

This may be too advanced for you, so if you do not understand this, then do your current line-by-line processing, but you must modify it to get your 4 columns.

So the code, which uses the pathlib.Path module and my regular expression, would look something like:

import csv
import re
from pathlib import Path

p = Path('/home/work_dir/FLrods')
input_paths = (file_path for file_path in p.glob('*') if file_path.is_file())

rex = re.compile(r'holdrod\s*=\s*(\S+)[\s\S]*measburn_tot\s*=\s*(\S+)')

with open('output.csv', 'w', newline='') as outputCSV:
    writer = csv.writer(outputCSV)
    writer.writerow(['header1', 'header2', 'header3', 'header4'])
    for input_path in input_paths:
        text = input_path.read_text()
        m = rex.search(text)
        if m:
            writer.writerow(['holdrod =', m[1], 'measburn_tot =', m[2]])

Q: CodeIgniter query builder script to GROUP BY gender and COUNT() rows in a table A:

A potential drawback with simply using GROUP BY and COUNT() in this scenario is that while the database is scarcely populated, there is the likelihood that not all (expected) genders will be represented in the result set.

There are also considerations of whether:

  • NULL is a possible value (when it is an optional profile field) or
  • the value is freehand (not constrained by a predefined list) or
  • users are allowed to abstain from answering the question or
  • non-binary values will be amalgamated into a catch-all "Other" in the results.

The following attempts to provide a more robust framework for addressing fringe scenarios to provide a stable/predictable result set.

By using a subquery of predefined values then LEFT JOINing the real data to it, the number of rows becomes predictable.

Query builder:

$sub = implode(
    ' UNION ALL ',
    array_map(
        fn($opt) => $this->db->select($this->db->escape($opt) . ' gender')->get_compiled_select(),
        ['Male', 'Female', 'Other', 'Unknown']
    )
);

return array_column(
    $this->db
        ->select(['g.gender', 'COUNT(*) total'])
        ->join(
            'personaldata p',
            "CASE
                 WHEN p.gender IN ('Male','M') THEN 'Male'
                 WHEN p.gender IN ('Female','F') THEN 'Female'
                 WHEN p.gender IS NOT NULL THEN 'Other'
                 ELSE 'Unknown'
             END = COALESCE(g.gender, 'Unknown')",
            'left',
            false
        )
        ->group_by('g.gender')
        ->order_by('gender')
        ->get("($sub) g")
        ->result(),
    'total',
    'gender'
);

This will return a flat, associative array of gender-count elements.

Rendered SQL (I added spacing for readability): SQLize Demo

SELECT `g`.`gender`, COUNT(*) total
FROM (
    SELECT 'Male' gender
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Female'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Other'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Unknown'
) g
LEFT JOIN personaldata p ON CASE
             WHEN p.gender IN ('Male','M') THEN 'Male'
             WHEN p.gender IN ('Female','F') THEN 'Female'
             WHEN p.gender IS NOT NULL THEN 'Other'
             ELSE 'Unknown'
         END = COALESCE(g.gender, 'Unknown')
GROUP BY `g`.`gender`
ORDER BY `gender`

Related: How to JOIN with ON CASE in Codeigniter

Q: Get the file size of a file to download using wget before wget-ing it A:

I was actually looking for the size of a directory and Google Search_ got me here. While there isn’t any direct answer here, the accepted answer helped me to build the following command on top of it:

wget --spider -m -np URL-to-dir 2>&1 | sed -n -e /unspecified/d -e '/^Length: /{s///;s/ .*//;p}' | paste -s -d+ | bc

The above runs wget in a spider mode for the entire directory, which ends up logging the length for each file in that directory. The output is then piped to sed to extract a sequence of numbers (byte sizes). The last two components in the pipe simply help sum it up to get the total in bytes.

Q: VS Code: enable inline spell checker, but disable spell check in the "Problems" panel A:

First, go to the setting at the bottom-left side of the Visual Studio Code window:

Search for "spell" in the search bar,
